prompt: What was the primary runtime cost that JSI eliminates compared to React Native's legacy bridge?
choices: The need to write any native code at all
JSON serialization of every argument/return value plus asynchronous queued dispatch across the bridge
The JavaScript thread's garbage collector
Support for TypeScript type checking

prompt: In JSI, how does a native module expose a callable method to JavaScript without going through a message queue?
choices: By registering a REST endpoint the JS thread polls
By serializing the method signature into a .proto file
By implementing a HostObject whose get() returns a Function created from a C++ host function, installed directly as a JS global/property
By writing the method in JavaScript and transpiling it to C++

prompt: Historically, why did Skia (via its Ganesh GPU backend) cause visible jank the first time a new shape/effect combination appeared on screen?
choices: Skia redraws the entire screen on every frame regardless of changes
The exact shader for that draw-state combination hadn't been seen before, so it was compiled on the render thread at that moment
Flutter's widget tree has to be rebuilt from scratch for new effects
The Dart garbage collector pauses during GPU operations

prompt: How does Impeller avoid the runtime shader-compilation jank that affected Skia?
choices: It disables shaders entirely and uses only solid colors
It enumerates the needed shader variants ahead of time and compiles them at engine-build time (via impellerc) into backend-specific bytecode bundled with the app
It compiles shaders on a background thread so the jank is invisible
It downloads precompiled shaders from a CDN on first launch

A MemberExpression whose object is an Identifier named 'NativeModules'

They are lazily loaded and called synchronously through direct host-object bindings instead of being eagerly initialized and invoked over the async JSON bridge
They no longer need to be registered with the native module registry
